# Weekly roll-up ruling (e2e agentic synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on how the week's reactions reach people:

> the per-run bundle stays, and on Fridays we add one roll-up of the week —
> what moved, what is still open — instead of asking anyone to scroll back

Tina asked whether the roll-up replaces the per-run bundle. Tanya held that it
does not: the bundle is for the run, the roll-up is for the week. Rejected: a
daily digest, because most days carry a single run and it would repeat the
bundle word for word.

payload.rationale: The document is a communication-cadence ruling by Tanya: per-run bundle stays, weekly roll-up added on Fridays, daily digest rejected. The most load-bearing narratives are DecisionsEvaporate (the roll-up explicitly replaces scroll-back) and DecisionCaptureAtConsensus (the per-run bundle is the capture artifact at consensus). I expanded AntiSlackPositioning and its children (AntiPatternRealtimeChat, Sprint4ThesisProven, ProductCategoryAsyncPlatform, pricing positions, target market) because the roll-up extends the anti-Slack thesis and the product's async-platform identity. ContextPreservationNextSprint, WebhookArchitecture, and ZephyrIntegrationUnlock are included because the roll-up is delivered through the same capture-and-delivery pipeline. Both style observations (DirectQuote, ShortPunchyCadence) match this document's quoted-ruling format. Both source samples are included for provenance. No areas were deliberately skipped — the graph is small and every node plausibly overlaps this document's product, decision, and style context.
